signals.text: SpaceX's CFO says it closed another AI hosting deal worth about $1.11B a month from Dec 1 (about $13B of annualized revenue) with a customer he did not name; he described its hosting deals as essentially 90-day terms with a 90-day out (verified fact: CFO on the record). Our X4 ruling: planned capacity, not a trip; the unnamed buyer remains the lead.

Anthropic commits about $11.6B over seven-year terms for dedicated Akamai cloud capacity. Akamai issues it a warrant for preferred stock convertible into up to about 7.7M common shares (about 5% of Akamai, per TechCrunch); later tranches vest with each further $3B Anthropic commits, up to $9B more (verified fact: Akamai 8-K, filed Sept 24).

Anthropic's draft prospectus (leaked, reviewed by Reuters) shows at least $518B of cloud, compute and infrastructure commitments over about a decade, about 80% payable regardless of use: Broadcom equipment leases about $161.2B, Google at least $111.1B, Amazon $110B, SpaceX/xAI up to $84.5B through 2029 (mostly cancelable on 90 days' notice), Microsoft $31.4B, AMD expected to exceed $20B. A draft prospectus, not a public SEC filing (credible report, via InvestmentNews).

OpenAI is in early talks to raise at least $30B at a valuation of about $1.4T before the new money, up from $852B in March; Altman has said it will not go public in 2026 (credible report: Bloomberg, via Reuters).

Tencent reportedly agreed this year to a five-year lease of about 100,000 advanced AI chips in Oracle data centers in Southeast Asia, worth about $7B (credible report: FT, via Reuters, which could not verify it). Buyer and seller are named, so this is not an X4 candidate.

Anthropic's draft prospectus shows Broadcom agreed to lend it up to $42B in convertible notes, which could finance about a third of a $125.2B five-year lease of TPU capacity; Anthropic deposited cash in a restricted account for Broadcom's benefit in April 2026, and the draft warns of 'potential conflicts of interest' because Broadcom is both supplier and lender (credible report: Reuters, via The Star; Broadcom did not comment, Anthropic declined). A draft prospectus, not a public SEC filing.

SoftBank invested the third and final $10B tranche of its $30B follow-on investment in OpenAI, through Vision Fund 2, bringing its cumulative investment to $64.6B for an ownership interest of about 13% (verified fact: SoftBank Group release).

Amazon is seeking to move about $8B of Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips, installed in more than a dozen US data centers, into a special-purpose vehicle that would raise outside debt (with up to 10% equity on offer), and to lease them back (credible report: people familiar, via the Financial Times, via Reuters, via The Standard; Amazon and Nvidia did not immediately respond). A named owner and chips already installed, so not an X4 candidate (our inference).

SpaceX is seeking to raise $40B to buy Nvidia AI chips, about $10B in bank loans and $30B in investment-grade debt (credible report: people familiar, via Reuters, via The Star). The Financial Times reported it first and that Apollo is expected to lead (credible report, via Reuters). SpaceX and Nvidia did not immediately comment; Apollo and PIMCO declined. A named buyer and a planned purchase, so not an X4 candidate (our inference); the reports do not tie it to SpaceX's unnamed hosting customer from Dec 1.

Broadcom is arranging more than $50B of financing for the custom AI chips it is building with OpenAI; Apollo and Blackstone are among the lenders approached, talks are early and the size could change (credible report: the Wall Street Journal, via Yahoo Finance; none of the companies has commented). Yahoo Finance notes that the WSJ did not say who would borrow. A named buyer and seller and a planned purchase, so not an X4 candidate (our inference).

The Information reports that Anthropic has committed to lease 15 gigawatts of data center capacity from Amazon Web Services, Google, SpaceX's SpaceXAI and other cloud providers and, citing people familiar with the relationship, that it has signed a multiyear cloud deal with Iren (credible report: The Information, via MT Newswires, via Yahoo Finance; MT Newswires files it as market chatter that may include rumor and speculation, and Anthropic, Hut 8, Iren, Google and SpaceX did not immediately respond to it). A named buyer and planned capacity, so not an X4 candidate (our inference).

Volta, an AI infrastructure company founded in February, is marketing $5B of debt for a data center in Norway and relies on Anthropic to buy much of its compute; Apollo anchors the deal with a $1.5B order, it is expected to price with a rate of at least 11%, some investors said they are already full up on data-center debt, and the rate falls if Anthropic gets an investment-grade credit rating (credible report: people familiar, via Semafor; JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs and Apollo declined to comment, and Volta and Anthropic did not respond). A named buyer and planned capacity, so not an X4 candidate (our inference).

NTT Data Group is in the final stages of talks to build a data center in Osaka, western Japan, for Anthropic, which would be Anthropic's first dedicated data center in Japan; it could cost $6.3B to build and partly open by 2028 (credible report: multiple sources, via Nikkei Asia). A named buyer and planned capacity, so not an X4 candidate (our inference).

Anthropic is seeking a valuation of more than $2T (credible report: Reuters, via CTech), and some prospective investors put its fair value at $1.8T to $2T (credible report: Bloomberg, via The Next Web). Its Series H on May 28 was at $965B post-money (verified fact: Anthropic). Roughly double in under five months, alongside reported revenue growth: a public valuation jump, not a hidden-capability signal (our inference).

CoreWeave's April-issued bonds fell to 79.15 cents on the dollar (Tradeweb data, via Reuters), a yield of around 15%, and the cost of insuring its debt rose to around 1,000 basis points, which Reuters says implies a nearly 63% chance of default in five years; its shares fell as much as 8.3% to their lowest since May 2025 before trading 5% higher (credible report: Reuters, via Investing.com). Strain in compute financing, not a sign of hidden compute (our inference).

Microsoft ended its agreement to anchor a flagship Nscale data centre in Loughton, Essex (23,040 Nvidia GB300 GPUs, 50 MW), after grid officials told Nscale they did not expect to supply power until the 2030s (credible report: Reuters, via Investing.com; The Telegraph reported it first). Microsoft said 'This decision relates to a single site' and that it remains committed to its Nscale partnership (Microsoft spokesperson, via Reuters); Nscale said the grid issue had no impact on its other contracts (Nscale, via Reuters). Cancelled capacity with a named buyer and a stated cause, so not an X4 candidate (our inference).

OpenAI is racing to secure investor commitments for a round that could value it at over $1.4T, per two people familiar; the round is about $30B, per one of them, and OpenAI told investors it had reached $50B in annualized revenue, per one of the people (credible report: Reuters, via Investing.com; OpenAI and SoftBank declined to comment).

Nscale is in talks to sell Anthropic computing power for a second facility at its Monarch data center campus in West Virginia, in a deal that could be worth about $45B (credible report: people familiar with the negotiations, via Bloomberg News, via Bloomberg Law); per Bloomberg, a regulatory filing for Nscale's planned IPO puts Anthropic's existing agreements with Nscale at up to about $44.6B (via Bloomberg; we have not opened the filing). Named buyer and seller and planned capacity, so not an X4 candidate (our inference).

SpaceX's Q3 results: Super Intelligence (SI) segment revenue of $7.56B, up 830% from a year earlier, driven mainly by new cloud services agreements, the Cursor acquisition and Grok adoption; SI capital spending of $16.44B in the quarter ($40.0B in the first nine months); and 1.7 GW of nameplate compute at Sept 30, up from 1.4 GW at June 30 (verified fact: SpaceX 8-K, Exhibit 99.1). Reuters reports the AI business earns revenue from compute contracts with Anthropic, Google and Reflection AI (credible report: Reuters, via NBC News; no source given). Named seller and named buyers, so not an X4 candidate (our inference).

The Wall Street Journal, which obtained a draft of Anthropic's S-1, reports about $450B of mostly noncancellable agreements with cloud providers, first-half 2026 revenue of $16.3B (from $1.1B a year earlier) and a first-half net loss of $80B (from $13B) (credible report: draft prospectus, via the WSJ, via Fortune). A draft prospectus, not a public SEC filing; the reports do not say whether the $450B covers the same commitments as the 'at least $518B' reported on Sept 28 (our inference). A named buyer, so not an X4 candidate (our inference).

Meta's non-cancelable contractual commitments reached $454.52B at Sept 30, up from $349.31B at June 30 (about $105B more in one quarter, our arithmetic), mostly third-party cloud capacity, servers and network infrastructure, data-center energy agreements and Reality Labs hardware, with about $45.85B due in 2026 and $121.41B in 2027; Meta also has contingent obligations to buy up to $14.72B of cloud capacity over five years, unchanged since June 30 (verified fact: Meta 10-Qs for Q2 and Q3). A named buyer, so not an X4 candidate (our inference).

SpaceX's Q3 10-Q says an unnamed 'Customer B', whose revenue relates to the SI segment, accounted for 34.5% of Q3 consolidated revenue of $14.58B, about $5.0B (our arithmetic), and reports a backlog of $62.96B at Sept 30, about 67% of it expected within a year (verified fact: SpaceX 10-Q). The filing does not name the customer; Reuters' list of SpaceX compute customers (Anthropic, Google, Reflection AI) and the SpaceX/xAI commitment in Anthropic's draft prospectus make one of those named labs the likely customer, so this is a lead to resolve and does not meet alarm condition X4 (our inference). Its Q3 revenue cannot come from the hosting deal worth about $1.11B a month that starts Dec 1, though the same customer could be behind both (our inference).

OpenAI is working on raising up to $30B at a $1.25T pre-money valuation, in a round led by Coatue and investors in the UAE that could be coupled with a deal for more computing capacity; terms are still being negotiated (credible report: sources, via CNBC, via TechCrunch; OpenAI declined to comment). That is below the about $1.4T reported on Sept 29 and the over $1.4T reported on Oct 19 (our inference); its March round valued it at $852B post-money (via TechCrunch).

DeepSeek has reportedly raised about $15B (about 100 billion yuan), with potential investors including CATL and Tencent (credible report: Bloomberg, via TechCrunch; DeepSeek did not immediately respond to TechCrunch); TechCrunch gives no valuation, calls it one of the biggest funding rounds in China and notes it came two days after the US ordered federal civilian agencies to remove DeepSeek's AI technology from their systems (via TechCrunch). A named lab raising capital, so not an X4 candidate (our inference).

Anthropic's public S-1 puts its expected future fixed or minimum guaranteed purchase commitments, mostly cloud hosting and other third-party infrastructure, at about $265.6B at June 30, 2026 (unaudited). It also reports new and amended agreements after June 30 with about $245B of future minimum payments, some subject to contractual conditions, plus about $21B of minimum payments under short-term agreements. Named commitments include at least $44.9B with Microsoft (Nov 2026 to May 2033), at least about $114.5B with Google (Apr 2026 to Jul 2033), at least $110B with Amazon (May 2026 to Apr 2036) and up to $120.5B with SpaceXAI, formerly X.AI LLC, into 2029. The SpaceXAI figure is about $3.1B a month once all capacity is delivered, which Anthropic expects in December 2026, and after initial periods ending in January and March 2027 either party can cancel each agreement on 90 days' notice. On top of that is an estimated $125B to $150B for more TPU compute delivered in 2028 to 2031, which is not in its commitments table (verified fact: Anthropic S-1). The S-1 leaves its own total committed spend blank, and because the $245B includes amended agreements the figures may overlap, so we do not add them up (our inference). Named buyer and sellers, so not an X4 candidate (our inference). It confirms Anthropic as a SpaceXAI compute customer, which narrows the SpaceX 'Customer B' lead of Oct 22 but does not settle it (our inference).

Microsoft's 10-Q for the quarter to Sept 30 records $10.0B of revenue from commercial arrangements with OpenAI, including revenue-sharing payments. Its accounts receivable from OpenAI rose to $7.2B from $6.0B at June 30, it has paid in $12.0B of its $13.0B funding commitment, and it booked $272M of net gains from its OpenAI investments, against $4.1B of net losses a year earlier (verified fact: Microsoft 10-Q). Named buyer and seller, so not an X4 candidate (our inference).

Microsoft priced $25B of notes in ten tranches due 2028 to 2066 (trade date Oct 29, settling Nov 4). Its preliminary prospectus supplement says the proceeds are for general corporate purposes, which may include working capital, capital expenditures, share repurchases, acquisitions and debt repayment, and does not tie them to AI (verified fact: Microsoft pricing term sheet and preliminary prospectus supplement; the $25B total is our arithmetic from the tranche sizes). Debt that may help fund the capex build, from a named borrower, so not an X4 candidate (our inference).

Anthropic's first S-1/A reports purchase commitments and lease agreements, including short-term commitments and leases not yet commenced, with an aggregate committed spend of about $895.4B as of and after Sept 30, 2026, substantially all of it compute and infrastructure: about $447.5B expected before the end of 2030, substantially all of the rest from 2031 to 2045, and about $69.8B due in the 12 months after Sept 30. Its Q3 2026 compute and infrastructure expense was $9,863M on revenue of $16,956M, and it had $146.6B of liquidity at Sept 30, including $14.8B available under its credit facility (verified fact: Anthropic S-1/A). The Oct 26 S-1 gave about $265.6B of commitments at June 30 plus about $245B of later agreements (verified fact: Anthropic S-1); the two filings word the basis differently, so we do not compute a change (our inference). A named buyer and mostly future capacity, so not an X4 candidate (our inference).

Oracle launched a $10B common stock offering and a concurrent $10B notes offering; the notes priced on Nov 2 in five tranches due 2029 to 2046, with coupons from 7.000% to 8.650% (the 2029 notes at 240 basis points over Treasuries) and expected ratings of Baa2 with a negative outlook (Moody's), BBB- (S&P) and BBB (Fitch), and the stock offering's prospectus supplement says the proceeds of both offerings are for general corporate purposes, which may include capital expenditures (verified fact: Oracle preliminary prospectus supplement and pricing term sheet; the five tranches sum to $10B, our arithmetic). Equity and borrowing by a named company, not capex, so not an X4 candidate (our inference).

Meta priced $15.0B of senior notes in five tranches due 2031 to 2056, with coupons from 5.850% to 7.500% (trade date Nov 3, settlement date Nov 5), and on Nov 4 priced EUR 9.0B of euro notes in six tranches due 2031 to 2065 (settlement date Nov 12); the term sheets give S&P's rating as AA- with a negative outlook and Moody's as Aa3, stable (verified fact: Meta pricing term sheets; the $15.0B and EUR 9.0B totals are our sums). Borrowing by a named company, not capex, so not an X4 candidate (our inference).

Riot Platforms signed a 15-year, 910 critical-IT-MW triple-net powered land lease for its whole Corsicana campus with an unnamed 'leading Frontier AI Lab', about $28B of contract value and about $1.8B of average annual rent, delivered as 400 MW in Sept 2027, 200 MW in Jan 2028 and 310 MW in July 2028; the tenant will own and operate the compute, rent is due on the full 910 MW whatever the use, and Riot says it is the same lab as its Rockdale lease earlier this year (verified fact: Riot Q3 2026 release, 8-K exhibit 99.1). Riot does not name the lab. Planned capacity, which X4 does not count, so not an X4 candidate; who the tenant is remains open (our inference).

Oracle has cancelled its chip-leasing contract with Tencent, the five-year lease of about 100,000 advanced AI chips in Oracle data centers in Southeast Asia, worth an estimated $7B, after bowing to pressure from the Trump administration; officials from Guangdong, where Tencent is based, asked Tencent to support domestic Chinese chips (credible report: people familiar, via the Financial Times, via Reuters, via Euronext; Reuters could not immediately verify it, and Oracle, Tencent and the White House did not respond to its requests for comment). It follows our Sept 30 signal; named parties, so not an X4 candidate (our inference).

Microsoft has tightened oversight of some data-center projects from the neocloud providers Nebius, IREN and Nscale, stepping away from projects it deems risky, debating internally whether to sign new neocloud deals (though it has not fully ruled them out) and not exercising an option to more than double its existing agreement with Nscale to rent more computing power at a Texas data center (credible report: people familiar, via Bloomberg News, via Reuters, via Investing.com). A Microsoft spokesperson said its infrastructure approach is built on flexibility and optionality, and Nebius and Nscale did not respond (via Reuters). IREN's 10-Q, filed Nov 5, says it is making a Microsoft-requested network design change across its Horizon deployments, with delivery dates extended without delay credits (verified fact: IREN 10-Q). A named buyer, so not an X4 candidate (our inference).

Anthropic's planned $1.5T IPO valuation faces mounting resistance from institutional investors after a sector-wide selloff in AI stocks; one investor suggested the pricing may fall closer to $1T, and backers are debating whether Anthropic should adjust its price range or delay; it had been targeting an offering the week before Thanksgiving to raise up to $100B (credible report: unnamed investors, via the Wall Street Journal, via Investing.com on Yahoo Finance). Anthropic has not published a price range (verified fact: S-1/A).

Some prospective investors are discussing a valuation of about $1.2T to $1.3T for Anthropic's IPO, down from the $1.4T to $1.5T range investors had earlier communicated to bankers; no final decisions have been made (credible report: a person familiar, via Bloomberg News, via Investing.com; an Anthropic spokesperson declined to comment).

OpenAI received $11B, the first part of a new funding round that values it at $1.25T; the round could grow to $20B in total in the coming weeks, after OpenAI first sought $30B or more at a $1.4T valuation and scaled back amid the AI stock selloff (credible report: people familiar, via Bloomberg, via Investing.com). The report does not say whether $1.25T is pre- or post-money; our Oct 22 signal had it as pre-money (via CNBC, via TechCrunch).

Microsoft is turning off AI computing capacity it rented from Oracle after declining to renew the contract, an arrangement announced in 2023 to power an AI-assisted version of Bing; the rented computing, which used older-generation Nvidia chips, no longer fit Microsoft's specifications, and the deal's full size could not be determined (credible report: people familiar, via Bloomberg on Yahoo Finance). An Oracle spokesperson said demand for its AI infrastructure remains strong, including for earlier-generation GPUs, and Microsoft declined to comment (via Bloomberg on Yahoo Finance). Named parties and a reduction, not a purchase, so not an X4 candidate (our inference).

Google acquired Crusoe's southeast Wyoming data-center site, which Crusoe and Tallgrass Energy had been developing; Crusoe gives no price or capacity, says the sale completes its pre-development work, and describes a planned power mix of fuel cells, grid power and natural-gas turbines (verified fact: Crusoe release). Named buyer and planned capacity, so not an X4 candidate (our inference).

Anthropic struck a deal worth about $3.4B for commitments on 1.7 GW of heavy-duty gas-fired generators for data centers, bought in late September from OnePWR Solutions, a San Antonio equipment supplier (credible report: the Financial Times, via Reuters on CNBC). Reuters could not immediately verify it, and Anthropic and OnePWR did not respond to requests for comment (via Reuters on CNBC). Named buyer and seller, so not an X4 candidate (our inference).

Anthropic's S-1/A No. 2 sets an IPO price range of $70 to $78 a share for 825M Class A shares on Nasdaq ('ANT') and a concurrent $26.0B private placement of non-voting Class N shares at the IPO price with seven chip and cloud companies: at the $74 midpoint, Google and Nvidia about $10.0B each, AMD about $2.5B, Broadcom, Micron and Microsoft about $1.0B each and TSMC about $500M; Google's part funds part of an investment it had already committed. Net proceeds from both would be about $84.6B at the midpoint. Its aggregate committed spend, substantially all compute and infrastructure, is about $900.9B as of and after Sept 30 (about $451.6B before the end of 2030 and about $70.7B due in the 12 months after Sept 30), against about $895.4B in the first S-1/A (verified fact: Anthropic S-1/A No. 2 and first S-1/A). On the 13,086,672,593 shares the prospectus says will be outstanding after the offering and the placement, the range values Anthropic at about $916B to $1.02T (our arithmetic); Reuters puts it at up to $1.02T (credible report: Reuters, via NBC News) and Fortune at up to $1.4T on a fully diluted basis (credible report: Fortune), against $965B post-money in the May Series H (verified fact: Anthropic). Google and Microsoft are also counterparties in its compute commitments (verified fact: Anthropic S-1), so part of the placement money would flow back to them as compute spending (our inference). Named parties, so not an X4 candidate (our inference).

CoreWeave's revenue backlog was about $132.5B at Sept 30; it expects 2026 capex of $37B to $39B and revenue of $13.0B to $13.3B, has over 1.7 GW of active and over 4.6 GW of contracted power, and its CEO cited about $9B of customer prepayments and deposits expected in the next three months (verified fact: CoreWeave Q3 release). Customers it names as expanding include OpenAI, Jane Street, Cohere and Perplexity. Named customers, so not an X4 candidate (our inference).

Nvidia's board accepted Jensen Huang's resignation as president, CEO and director, effective immediately; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO and stays CFO, and Harvey C. Jones becomes chair (verified fact: Nvidia 8-K, date of report Nov 11, and Nvidia release, Nov 12). Neither gives a reason or says anything about his equity or severance, and the release keeps Q3 FY2027 results on Nov 17 as previously scheduled (verified fact: Nvidia 8-K and release). On Nov 8 the board had opened an independent investigation of reporting that Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort (verified fact: Nvidia board statement). CNBC reports that he resigned after two extramarital affairs were made public, and that Nvidia shares fell 11% in the week to Nov 12 (credible report: CNBC). A departure at the main AI chip supplier, but no equity given up on the record, so not an X4 candidate (our inference).

Anthropic's IPO has drawn about six times the orders for the shares available, and the shares are expected to begin trading on Nasdaq on Nov 19; bankers told prospective investors that Anthropic will prioritize its existing backers, leaving some would-be buyers with smaller allocations than expected (credible report: Bloomberg News and people familiar, via Reuters on Investing.com; Anthropic could not immediately be reached for comment). Anthropic's IPO website, a free writing prospectus dated Nov 10, says the final IPO price is expected to be determined on Nov 18, Eastern time, and the range in the filing is unchanged so far (verified fact: Anthropic free writing prospectus and EDGAR, read 13:37 PT Nov 13, no later amendment).

Nscale's S-1/A of Nov 12 says Anthropic exercised, on Sept 29, its right to contract for more compute at Building 2 of Nscale's Monarch campus; the two have 60 days, subject to mutual extension, to negotiate an agreement, after which Nscale may contract Building 2 to someone else, and once a Building 2 agreement is signed Anthropic may exercise a further right on Building 3. The filing also says GPU services agreements signed with Anthropic on Aug 25 provide for payments of up to about $44.6B for Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 deployments at Monarch, and that Microsoft statements of work signed between Sept 2025 and April 2026 provide for up to about $43.8B through Dec 2033, of which one statement of work worth $3.22B was later terminated; it gives no value for Building 2 (verified fact: Nscale S-1/A). If the 60 days run from Sept 29, they end about Nov 28 unless extended (our arithmetic). This follows our Oct 20 signal on talks for a second Monarch facility worth about $45B (via Bloomberg). Named buyer and seller, so not an X4 candidate (our inference).

Nebius's Q3 2026 shareholder letter gives Q3 capex of about $7.3B, now expects 2026 capex of about $27B, above its $20B to $25B range, and gives an initial 2027 outlook of $40B to $45B of capital expenditures, 'sized for more than 1 GW of new capacity', 75% to 85% of it to be funded by prepayments and asset-backed financing of existing investment-grade contracts, with more than 4 GW of power contracted and 5 GW expected by year-end; it says prepayments on deals signed in Q3 covered over 100% of the associated capex (verified fact: Nebius Q3 2026 shareholder letter). Named company, mostly planned capacity, so not an X4 candidate (our inference).

OpenAI has raised $15B at a $1.25T valuation (credible report: sources, via CNBC's Kate Rooney, video report); CNBC's page names no investors and does not say whether $1.25T is pre- or post-money. It is likely the same round as the $11B first part reported on Nov 6, now larger, and we found no announcement by OpenAI on Nov 13 (our inference).

SpaceX plans to invest more than $74B in two supercomputing campuses, more than $24B at Starbase, Texas, and about $50B in Cochise County, Arizona (credible report: SpaceX's statement, via Reuters on Investing.com); Reuters says the Arizona campus still needs county approval, with a public hearing set for December. Named investor and planned capacity, which X4 does not count, so not an X4 candidate (our inference).

notes: Capex is cash purchases of property and equipment and excludes finance leases, so it is lower than the 'capex including finance leases' headline some companies quote (Microsoft in particular; Meta's headline adds about $1B a quarter in lease principal). Amazon is gross, not net of incentives.
An independent read of each company's earnings releases matches the SEC XBRL-derived quarterly capex exactly.

Calendar Q3 2026 has now been reported by all four: Meta filed its 10-Q on Oct 22, Microsoft on Oct 28, Alphabet on Oct 29 and Amazon on Oct 30 (EDGAR filing dates, read Oct 30); the capex figures come only from scripts/update_sec.py. Nvidia reports Q3 FY2027 (the quarter ended Oct 25, 2026) on Nov 17, 2026, with results at about 1:20 p.m. PT and its call at 2 p.m. PT, a date its Nov 12 CEO-transition release keeps 'as previously scheduled' (Nvidia, Oct 28 and Nov 12); until then the newest Nvidia data-center figure is FY2027 Q2.

Anthropic, PBC filed a public S-1 on Oct 26, 2026, its first amendment (S-1/A) on Nov 2 and a second (S-1/A No. 2) on Nov 10, followed by five free writing prospectuses accepted Nov 10 to Nov 12 (EDGAR, CIK 0002130357, read 13:37 PT Nov 13, with no later amendment and no final prospectus yet); EDGAR also lists its earlier draft registration statements (a DRS on June 1 and five DRS/A, July 13 to Oct 9). S-1/A No. 2 sets an estimated price range of $70.00 to $78.00 a share for 825,000,000 Class A shares (801,351,354 sold by Anthropic and 23,648,646 by selling stockholders, with an underwriters' option on 123,750,000 more), to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market as 'ANT', plus a concurrent $26.0B private placement of non-voting Class N shares at the IPO price; it gives Run-Rate Revenue of about $81B at Oct 31, 2026 and an aggregate committed spend of about $900.9B, against about $895.4B in the first S-1/A (verified fact: EDGAR, S-1/A No. 2 and the first S-1/A). Anthropic's IPO website, filed as a free writing prospectus dated Nov 10, says the final IPO price is expected to be determined on Nov 18, Eastern time (verified fact: Anthropic free writing prospectus). Where a filing gives a figure we cite it; figures still labelled 'draft prospectus' come from the leaked draft as reported by Reuters, Fortune, the FT and the WSJ (via Fortune). The shares are expected to begin trading on Nasdaq on Nov 19, and the offering has drawn about six times the orders for the shares available (credible report: Bloomberg News, via Reuters on Investing.com, Nov 12).
Run-rates annualize one recent period and are often floors; they are not comparable with quarterly revenue and are never plotted on the same axis.

Kalshi's 'any company before Apr 1, 2027' market stood at 15% on Nov 13, 2026 (Pacific) (live API: last trade 15 at 05:33 PT Nov 13, bid/ask 14/15 at 13:14 PT; not thin by our rule, with about 38.2k contracts traded, though only about 14 contracts were offered at the ask), down from 18% on Nov 6, after 17% on Oct 30, 19% on Oct 23, 25% on Oct 9, 30% on Oct 2 and 32% on Sept 29. A widely repeated 62% figure from early September does not match the current price.

Anthropic's and OpenAI's run-rates are not like for like (our inference). Anthropic's S-1 says sales to customers through cloud-provider marketplaces made up about 47% of its 2025 revenue and 48% in the first half of 2026 (verified fact: Anthropic S-1), while per Reuters and the FT (via Investing.com), both Oct 8, OpenAI does not count revenue from sales through cloud partners (credible report).
method: Context, not a test. Capex is total cash purchases of property and equipment by Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta (mostly AI data centers; also non-AI spending such as Amazon logistics), summed by calendar quarter when all four have reported. The capability line is the best METR-measured frontier time horizon released by each quarter end; readings above 16 hours are beyond METR's reliable range, and quarters after METR's latest measurement can miss newer models. Models take months to train on new capacity, so spending often leads releases. Our actual test for hidden compute is alarm condition X4.
